title: Aftermath and Weather
premise: After her mother's funeral, Cyrus Coldharbour returns to the family house on the coast to catalog a lifetime of silence — seven years of estrangement, of things almost said. Sorting through tapes and photographs, she hears a song on a late-night radio program that she knows was written by her mother and never recorded. The broadcast pulls Cyrus into the orbit of the people who knew her mother before: a former bandmate, a half-sibling she never suspected, and a stranger in an old photograph who turns out to be the song's true co-author. As Cyrus traces the song's history toward its origin, she must forgive both the woman in the photographs and herself; the story ends with Cyrus performing the unfinished second verse at the house's last night before it is sold, finally saying what was never said.
about_author: Ada Kavanagh is the pen name of a writer raised in coastal fishing towns who spent a decade as an archivist before turning to fiction. Her work examines inheritance, music, and the silences families keep.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Cyrus arrives at the Coldharbour house three days after the funeral, tasked by the estate lawyer with cataloging its contents. In her mother Vera's locked studio she finds labeled boxes but no will, no letters. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: numb procedural grief masking seven years of unspoken apology.

chapters.title: Boxes of Weather
chapters.summary: Cyrus inventories the studio, finding reel-to-reel tapes marked only with dates and weather notes. A neighbor, Odile, mentions Vera played music 'for someone far away' every Sunday. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: first crack in the silence — grief becomes curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Radio Keeps
chapters.summary: Unable to sleep, Cyrus plays a tape while a radio murmurs behind her; the station's late host introduces a song called 'Aftermath and Weather' — one she watched Vera write and never record. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vertigo; the dead speaking through airwaves.

chapters.title: The Host at Night
chapters.summary: Cyrus calls the station; the host, Marlowe, says the recording came from a listener named Teodor Brandt, who claims co-authorship. Cyrus has never heard the name. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into need to know.

chapters.title: Stranger in the Photograph
chapters.summary: In a 1980s photo album Cyrus finds Vera young, laughing, arm around a man whose face is scratched out — the same man from the radio credits. POV: Cyrus, with a brief italicized memory of childhood questions deflected. Emotional beat: the mother begins to become a stranger worth knowing.

chapters.title: Odile Remembers Loudly
chapters.summary: Over fish stew, Odile recounts the summer Vera played harbor bars with a duo called Salt & Signal — and how Vera came back one autumn alone, pregnant, and burned her setlists. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: warmth that makes the family silence feel more deliberate.

chapters.title: Teodor Brandt, Address Unknown
chapters.summary: Marlowe agrees to forward a letter to his anonymous contributor. Cyrus writes three drafts, each angrier than the last, mails none — then mails the third after all. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: reckless honesty practiced for the first time.

chapters.title: The Half-Brother
chapters.summary: A reply comes not from Teodor but from a lawyer representing Ilya Coldharbour-Brandt, claiming to be Vera's son and heir to the song's rights. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: cold calculation hiding his own hunger to know Vera.

chapters.title: Two Heirs, One House
chapters.summary: Ilya arrives with paperwork; Cyrus counters with the fact that Vera left him nothing in any draft will she can find. They circle each other over coffee neither drinks. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: rivalry sharpened by shared abandonment.

chapters.title: Tape 14
chapters.summary: Alone, Cyrus plays Tape 14: Vera's voice rehearsing 'Aftermath and Weather,' stopping mid-verse, saying, 'He'll know why.' The second verse was never finished. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: devastation — the silence had a shape all along.

chapters.title: The Co-Author's Version
chapters.summary: Teodor finally calls the station; Marlowe relays his account: he and Vera wrote the song the winter before Cyrus was born, and parted when Vera chose the child over the road. POV: Marlowe framing Teodor's letter. Emotional beat: sympathy complicating blame.

chapters.title: Salt & Signal, Reassembled
chapters.summary: Cyrus tracks down the duo's old bassist, now a piano tuner, who reveals Teodor wasn't just a partner — he was the one Vera's family blamed for everything, wrongly. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the inheritance of other people's verdicts.

chapters.title: Ilya's Evidence
chapters.summary: Ilya produces letters proving Vera sent him money secretly for years — payments Cyrus never knew about, meaning Vera didn't abandon him entirely. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: his armor cracking; envy of Cyrus curdling into kinship.

chapters.title: The Scratched Face
chapters.summary: Cyrus carefully lifts the scratch on the photograph and finds writing beneath: not hatred but a date — the day Cyrus was born. Teodor was there. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the stranger in the photograph becomes family.

chapters.title: Running Out of Coast
chapters.summary: The estate sale is scheduled; a developer's offer looms. Cyrus and Ilya, uneasy allies now, petition for thirty days. The lawyer warns them the house will not wait longer. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: time becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Cyrus writes Vera a letter she'll never send, listing everything almost said across seven years — the fight, the wedding she skipped, the phone calls cut short. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: confession without absolution yet.

chapters.title: Teodor Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: An old man appears at the gate during rain: Teodor Brandt, dying, come to finish the verse or die trying. He and Cyrus recognize each other from the photograph instantly. POV: Teodor. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Winter It Was Written
chapters.summary: Teodor tells the whole story: the song was written for Vera's unborn child, and the unfinished second verse was hers to complete — she never could, because finishing it meant forgiving herself for choosing. POV: Teodor. Emotional beat: the weight of survival — someone always pays.

chapters.title: Ilya's Verse
chapters.summary: Ilya, who grew up on the recorded fragments, hums a melody he invented as a boy believing it was Vera's missing line. It fits. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: the disinherited son contributing the keystone.

chapters.title: Last Night in the House
chapters.summary: On the eve of the sale, Cyrus hosts the house's final gathering: Marlowe broadcasts live from the parlor, Odile cooks, Teodor tunes the old guitar. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: fragile communion built from wreckage.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Weather (Complete)
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Ilya, and Teodor perform the finished song together on air — Cyrus singing the second verse aloud, saying everything the seven years withheld. Listeners call in weeping; the house feels briefly like a held breath released. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax — forgiveness spoken, not just felt.

chapters.title: What Gets Inherited
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the house sold, the masters donated to the station archive, Cyrus and Ilya splitting not the money but the songwriting credit. Cyrus keeps only Tape 14 and the restored photograph. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen rather than inherited, and worth its price.
